title: The Island Due Back

plate.narration: Beneath the clouds, a low island comes into view. A notch breaks its flat brow. On the lookout, a bell waits beside folded signal cloths and a landing board.

goal.text: Help the keepers meet the island that is due back.

steps.label: Spot the island in the clouds

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.

npcVoices.Pip Thistledown: Eager manticore scout. Asks before guessing, repeats signals, and credits another observer.
npcVoices.Kitsune keeper: Practical, welcoming navigator. Uses songs alongside observations; never knows an unseen cause.

arrival.narration: Beyond the whales' turning place, a kitsune keeper stands beside a lookout bell. Pip Thistledown, the manticore scout, holds its rope clear of his tail. A flat island appears beneath the cloud. Beside you wait a folded landing board, signal cloths and a wooden box of song slips. "Help us meet that island," says the keeper. "It is due back. I expected more time to get the board out."

variants.text: The scattered cloud whales have not returned to the lookout. The keeper has lost the circling song she usually listens for before an island comes in. "We will need sightings from the ground," she says. Nobody claims to know where the whales went.

The cloud whales you guided clear are singing beyond the open lane. The keeper hears a turning note and points beneath the cloud. "They have seen something low. We should look there first." Their song offers a place to look, not a promise about where the island will stop.

return_song.narration: The keeper opens the song box. She taps a different shape on each slip as the welcome tune moves between them. Watch the song-shape pattern, then echo it while Pip searches beneath the cloud. "A song with directions," he says. "Much harder to lose than my map."

interaction.cue: Watch the welcome's shape pattern, then echo it.

onSuccess.narration: The keeper sings the shapes while your party checks the approaching outline.

onFailure.narration: The keeper holds the song slips open as a reference. You compare the shapes together instead of claiming to know the welcome by heart.

onAssisted.narration: The keeper sings the shapes while your party checks the approaching outline.

sightings.narration: A notch on the approaching island slides past a distant cloud break. The keeper plants two sighting sticks beside the lookout. "The clouds move too. Check the notch against the roof corner, or follow it through the cloud banks." Which sighting will you test?

choices.label: Compare the notch from two fixed viewpoints
Time the notch against the lookout roof
Use the guided whales' turning note

sightings_1.narration: Use the fixed roof corner to check when the moving notch passes it. Pip keeps yesterday's sketch out of the way.

sightings_1_check.narration: Track the approaching island from the marked ground. Use the fixed lookout corner or follow the notch through the moving cloud; a drifting cloud alone is no landmark.

interaction.cue: Mark the notch as it passes the fixed roof corner.

sightings_1_done.narration: Your two calls make a clear sequence: the island will pass below the left side of the lookout. The keeper moves the loose board to that side. A second sighting agrees. There is still work before a crossing, but the waiting place is no longer a guess.

sightings_1_changed.narration: A cloud hides the notch before your second call. You leave the missing sighting blank. The keeper keeps the board folded until the island comes fully into view; then she moves it to the left. Waiting costs preparation time, not anyone's footing.

sightings_2.narration: Follow the same notch through the moving cloud banks. The keeper points out its shape before the cloud hides it.

sightings_2_check.narration: Track the approaching island from the marked ground. Use the fixed lookout corner or follow the notch through the moving cloud; a drifting cloud alone is no landmark.

interaction.cue: Follow the marked notch-view through the cloud banks.

sightings_2_done.narration: Two careful counts put the island below the left side of the lookout. The keeper shifts the folded board there while the ground between you is clear. Pip ties a little knot in his string for the count; the knot is a note, not a mooring line.

sightings_2_changed.narration: Your first count follows the cloud instead of the notch. Pip catches the mismatch and lowers the string. You wait for the island to clear the mist, then the keeper moves the board to the left. Nobody turns an uncertain count into permission to cross.

priority.narration: A gust rattles the song box. A messenger's letter bag slides toward the low fence; a keeper has hold of the messenger herself. Your team can recover the sealed letters or ready the signal station. The other job must wait. Dry letters preserve a messenger departure; a ready station can send a temple signal. Which comes first?

choices.label: Recover the messenger bag before the next gust
Secure the song slips and signal station

priority_1.narration: The messenger points out her bag's strong strap. The other keepers cover the song slips while your party goes to the fence.

priority_2.narration: Your party takes the signal frame. The messenger stays with a keeper while her low bag waits for recovery.

letters.narration: The mailbag catches inside the fence. Reach its strong strap with a looped pole, or pass a hauling line toward the gate. The messenger points at the flap. "Not that bit. That bit is mostly wishes." Which way will you bring it in?

choices.label: Lift the strap with a looped pole
Draw the bag sideways along the fence
Have a duskrunner secure the bag strap

letters_1.narration: Reach the looped pole from the dry path. Aim at the strap the messenger pointed out, not the loose flap.

letters_1_check.narration: The mailbag hangs by its strap beside the fence. Reach with the looped pole from the marked ground. The letters are taking an unscheduled holiday.

interaction.cue: Tap when the marker reaches the gold.

letters_1_done.narration: The loop catches the strap and you lift the bag onto the path. The sealed letters are dry. Their owner hugs the bag, then checks the seal on each packet. She can leave with the first clear signal instead of spending the afternoon making replacements.

letters_1_changed.narration: The loop slips off as the gust changes. You draw the pole back. A keeper reaches the gate below and retrieves the bag after the wind settles, but water has entered one corner. The messenger keeps the sealed packets to dry; she cannot promise an immediate delivery.

letters_2.narration: Pass a hauling line along the inside fence toward the gate. The messenger can draw the bag sideways from there.

letters_2_check.narration: Pass the hauling line along the inside of the fence. The messenger draws the bag toward the gate while the keeper holds the slope clear.

interaction.cue: Pass the hauling line toward the fence gate.

letters_2_done.narration: The bag travels along the inside of the fence and comes through the gate. Every sealed letter is dry. The messenger checks them without opening them and offers to carry an authorized warning as soon as your signal is ready. Your rescue has saved her departure time.

letters_2_changed.narration: The line catches on the fence post. You stop instead of pulling the bag apart. The keeper below works it free later; one corner has soaked through. The messenger must dry the sealed packets before leaving, so a fast warning will need the lookout flags.

station.narration: The signal frame rocks in the wet grass. Level its weighted feet while the keeper covers the song box. The frame must turn freely for both cloths to show. A working frame will let you prepare a temple signal instead of packing a longer hand relay.

interaction.cue: Level the signal frame before securing its feet.

onSuccess.narration: The frame stands level. Both cloths turn freely.

onFailure.narration: A foot slides. You lower the frame and keep the song slips dry; messages will need a hand relay.

onAssisted.narration: The frame stands level. Both cloths turn freely.

station_1_done.narration: The frame stays level through the next gust. The keeper lifts both cloths and turns them toward the neighboring temple lookout; they fall freely when she lowers them. The song slips stay dry. You have a working station for a warning that must be seen quickly.

station_1_changed.narration: One foot slides in the wet grass. You lower the frame together and keep the box covered. The keeper will repair the footing before using it. Until then, signals must be carried by hand from the shelter; they will take an extra relay.

signal_plan.narration: The keeper lays out the cloths: white means watch; striped means stop. Pip can repeat your signal so you know it reached him, or keep watching the island while the keeper calls. Repeating will help with the later bearing; continuous watching follows the notch. Which job will you practice?

choices.label: Have Pip repeat each sign before anyone moves
Keep Pip watching the island and use the keeper's call

signal_plan_1.narration: Pass the striped stop signal along the marked ground. Pip repeats it only after it reaches him. The keeper waits for that echo before anyone uses the board.

interaction.cue: Catch the stop signal, then pass it to the next watcher.

onSuccess.narration: Every watcher echoes the stop before the next move.

onFailure.narration: Every watcher echoes the stop before the next move.

onAssisted.narration: Every watcher echoes the stop before the next move.

signal_plan_2.narration: Keep watching the island's notch through the cloud while the keeper gives the cloth calls. You gain one continuous view rather than a repeated signal; the normal measuring interval will still apply.

interaction.cue: Follow the notch-view without changing watchers.

onSuccess.narration: The keeper has a continuous sighting while she calls the cloths.

onFailure.narration: The keeper takes over the hidden sighting. You will use her second lookout for any unfinished measure.

onAssisted.narration: The keeper has a continuous sighting while she calls the cloths.

bearings.narration: The returning island clears the cloud with its flat shelf and stone's empty eye. The landing board fits only while the shelves are close. Compare its painted marks with the gap, or follow the shelves' movement. Your repeated signal, if practiced, gives a wider measuring interval. How will you check the approach?

choices.label: Compare the gap with the board's painted marks
Call the shelves' closest points together

bearings_1.narration: Compare the gap with the board's painted limit. Call the close interval from the lookout; the keeper will repeat the measure.

bearings_1_check.narration: Watch the two shelves from the lookout. Wait for their closest point, then call your measure. The keeper will repeat it before laying down the board. Nobody steps into the gap to test it.

interaction.cue: Tap in the gold when the shelves line up.

bearings_1_done.narration: Two measures agree on a narrow, steady gap. The keeper points to the painted limit that makes the board usable. Pip records where the shelves line up so the return can be checked too. You have verified a crossing window rather than guessed from one lucky glance.

bearings_1_changed.narration: Your two measures disagree. The keeper keeps the board back while the island slides a little farther past. She takes the next pair herself and finds a shorter window. You can still cross with her watching every step, but your own estimate is not marked as verified.

bearings_2.narration: Follow the shelf edge through the mist. Keep the same shelf in view while the keeper checks the gap.

bearings_2_check.narration: Watch the two shelves from the lookout. Wait for their closest point, then call your measure. The keeper will repeat it before laying down the board. Nobody steps into the gap to test it.

interaction.cue: Tap in the gold when the shelves line up.

bearings_2_done.narration: Your calls agree for two full beats. The keeper marks the board's safe limit and Pip notes the position for the return. The crossing window is small but checked by your observers. You can explain exactly which alignment you used without promising that it will last.

bearings_2_changed.narration: A gust covers one call. You stop the count instead of pretending everyone heard. The keeper takes a second set of observations and offers a shorter, supervised window. Your party can cross safely on her signals, but your own timing stays an unfinished test.

bearings_relay.narration: Use the repeated signal you practiced. The keeper's echoed call makes the close interval easier to follow.

bearings_relay_check.narration: Watch the two shelves from the lookout. Wait for their closest point, then call your measure. The keeper will repeat it before laying down the board. Nobody steps into the gap to test it.

interaction.cue: Tap in the gold when the shelves line up.

landing.narration: The keeper lays the board between the close shelves. A second keeper secures the far rope. You can center the near foot, or level the loaded board before following its side ropes. The keepers will watch the gap throughout your visit and call you back. Which job will you take?

choices.label: Steady the board while its foot is secured
Check the side ropes and guide careful steps
Have a thornguard brace the landing board

variants.text: Pip keeps your checked alignment ready for the return.
Your estimate is unfinished; the second lookout will call the return gap.

landing_1.narration: Watch the near foot while the keeper takes the tie. Center it before the party crosses with its kit.

landing_1_check.narration: The keeper secures the board foot while you watch its movement on the near shelf. Wait for its centered interval before she tightens the tie. Nobody crosses until the foot is fixed.

interaction.cue: Secure the board foot in its centered interval.

landing_1_done.narration: The board stays square while the keeper secures its foot. Your party crosses in order and waits behind the far rope. Pip brings up the end without jumping. The second keeper checks the alignment again before allowing the lookout helpers to cross after you.

landing_1_changed.narration: The gust shifts the board before its foot is secure. Everyone steps onto grass. You lift the board together. Before laying it again, your party must reduce the load or change how it carries the kit.

landing_2.narration: Level the loaded board while the keeper checks the side ropes. Follow her call across the steady span.

landing_2_check.narration: Keep the board level while the second keeper secures the far-side rope. Your party follows the checked side ropes across once the board is steady.

interaction.cue: Level the board before crossing with the kit.

landing_2_done.narration: The side ropes hold their clear line and each traveler can see the next handhold. The keeper keeps the board square while your party crosses. Pip waits until the last person is on grass before he moves. The helpers follow only after a fresh check of the gap.

landing_2_changed.narration: A side rope sags during the practice halt. You return to grass and lower the board. The keeper replaces the rope while your party decides what to carry on the next close alignment.

stone_care.narration: On the returning island, a round hole looks through an old standing stone. Grooves wind between three raised shapes below it. Pip crouches to move his shadow away. Choose a small job to prepare the reading place without touching a worn line.

interaction.cue: Prepare a place to read the stone.

options.label: Mark where readers can stand
options.reaction: Boots stay back from the worn stone face.

options.label: Move loose grass away from the tool place
options.reaction: The brush and sheet have a clean resting place.

options.label: Move your shadow off the grooves
options.reaction: Pip shifts sideways until the old lines are visible.

onSuccess.narration: The stone and the reading place are ready for a closer look.

onFailure.narration: The stone and the reading place are ready for a closer look.

onAssisted.narration: The stone and the reading place are ready for a closer look.

carving.narration: The shallow grooves are hard to separate from grass shadows. Brush loose dust, or hold a sheet as shade. Rounded carved edges cross a sharp later crack; keep uncertain parts dotted. A complete kit adds a broad copying frame. A borrowed pocket kit leaves that wider support behind. Which tool will you use?

choices.label: Brush loose dust and copy only clear grooves
Shade the face and copy it from the side

carving_1.narration: Brush loose dust beside the rounded grooves. Leave the sharp crack and any uncertain meeting point out of the solid copied line.

carving_1_check.narration: Guide the soft brush across the loose dust beside a carved groove. Keep clear of the sharp crack. Record only the rounded edges you can distinguish.

interaction.cue: Trace the clear carved edge, leaving the crack alone.

carving_1_done.narration: Loose dust falls away from the joined grooves. Their carved edges are rounded alike; the sharp crack cuts across both. You can show where the two old lines meet without drawing the crack into them. Pip leaves a dotted patch where the stone is still worn.

carving_1_changed.narration: Dust hides the meeting point. You stop before the brush catches a loose edge. The keeper can show you the broad pattern, but the little join stays dotted on your drawing. A readable clue does not require every worn line to become a confident new one.

carving_2.narration: Hold a sheet beside the stone to shade its face. The keeper points out rounded grooves while Pip copies them.

carving_2_check.narration: Hold the sheet as a shade while the keeper points out rounded grooves and the sharper crack. Keep the shade steady as Pip copies the visible distinction.

interaction.cue: Hold a steady shade beside the old stone.

carving_2_done.narration: In the even shade the two grooves meet cleanly beneath the eye. The crack stays sharp and separate. You copy both kinds of mark with different strokes. Pip points out the worn corner and you leave it dotted; the clearer join does not repair that missing piece.

carving_2_changed.narration: The sheet flickers in the gust. A shadow seems to join two lines, then moves away. You lower the sheet and copy the broad pattern with the keeper's help. The meeting point stays dotted so nobody later mistakes the shifting shadow for something carved.

orientation.narration: Three ridges show through the cloud below. Three raised marks sit on the stone. Keep the old rope groove at the top, then line up the lookout sketch and your copy without rotating either to force a match. Pip turns his head instead. "Very inconvenient for my theory."

interaction.cue: Set up the comparison before interpreting the lines.

options.label: Find the rope groove at the top

clues: Find the fixed top before orienting the pages.
Hold both pages upright before comparing their marks.
The ridge comparison comes after orientation.

onSuccess.narration: Your pages have a fixed top. Now test which marks and spaces agree.

onFailure.narration: The keeper points out the old rope groove and helps hold the pages upright. The interpretation is still your next job.

onAssisted.narration: Your pages have a fixed top. Now test which marks and spaces agree.

comparison.narration: Three raised marks appear on your copy beside today's three-ridge sketch. Grooves bend between the old marks, interrupted by a worn patch. Compare the ridge spacing or the channel's order. A clear copied join gives a wider scale target. Test the match before deciding what the spaces mean.

choices.label: Compare the order and spacing of the three ridges
Follow the channel past each fixed ridge
Use the clearly recorded carved join

variants.text: Your clear copy distinguishes the carved join from the crack.
The uncertain meeting point remains dotted on your copy.

comparison_1.narration: Keep both pages upright. Compare the ridge spaces with your stalk scale, leaving the worn patch untouched.

comparison_1_check.narration: Compare the spacing of the three ridge marks with the lookout sketch. Place the scale at the clear measuring interval. Do not fill the worn patch to make it fit.

interaction.cue: Match the scale to the checked ridge spacing.

comparison_1_done.narration: The ridge spaces fit without turning the paper. Between them, the carved surface continues across today's gaps. "So the land was joined here," Pip says. You keep the checked measurements and leave the date and cause blank.

comparison_1_changed.narration: The worn middle mark will not give a clean measure. You stop with two distances that disagree. The keeper leaves both papers in your hands. Which different comparison could your party try?

comparison_2.narration: Keep the fixed top in view while following the channel past each ridge. Do not let the reflection turn the paper for you.

comparison_2_check.narration: Follow the channel past the three fixed ridge marks. Watch the ridge-order pattern before the cloudy reflection covers it, then echo the order without inventing the missing bend.

interaction.cue: Watch the fixed-ridge pattern, then echo it.

comparison_2_done.narration: The fixed ridges appear in the same order in both views. The old surface continues between them where today's sketch has gaps: the land was joined here. Your checked order stays beside the copy. Its date and cause remain unknown.

comparison_2_changed.narration: The dotted patch hides the middle turn. You cannot finish that tracing. Pip lowers his measuring stalk and the keeper waits. Your party can try a different comparison without pretending the missing turn is visible.

alternative.narration: Pip looks from the stone to the lookout sketch. "The land was joined here. But when?" The stone and song give no date. Leave a question that would help another reader test what you found, without inventing who moved the land.

interaction.cue: Choose a useful next question.

options.label: What could date the carving?
options.reaction: The date stays open beside the copied shapes.

options.label: Could another view challenge the match?
options.reaction: The keeper marks a comparison another reader can test.

options.label: What could explain the change?
options.reaction: The cause remains unknown. The observation stays on the page.

onSuccess.narration: Your observation and unanswered questions remain separate.

onFailure.narration: Your observation and unanswered questions remain separate.

onAssisted.narration: Your observation and unanswered questions remain separate.

record.narration: The keeper asks permission to keep a copy of your observations. Your sketch can stay private or help other readers test the match. The stone stays here either way. What may she copy?

choices.label: Share the checked observations with their limits
Deliver the route report we promised the whale keeper

variants.text: Your independent comparison succeeded; a shared copy will credit its test.
A shared copy will credit the follow-up your party made with help. The unfinished test stays marked.
The promised whale report can be delivered separately from your stone sketch.

record_1.narration: You authorize a shared copy with its credit, missing detail and helped work marked. Pip keeps your original page beside it.

record_2.narration: Your sketch stays with your party. The keeper accepts that choice and keeps her own public-warning observations separate.

departure.narration: The temple roofs appear through the cloud ahead. The island is still moving toward them. "They should know," says Pip. Choose the first message: a course warning or an invitation to inspect the stone. Neither needs your private sketch. You will dispatch it after returning to the lookout.

choices.label: Send the temple a course warning first
Invite another keeper to inspect the stone first

variants.text: The messenger offers to carry this authorized message with her dry letters.
Your ready station has a temple dispatch slot.
The relay will leave after your party finishes returning the kit.
The whale report you promised is delivered and helps the next watcher. Your separate stone sketch was not included.

departure_1.narration: You choose the course warning first. The keeper prepares its direction and timing without adding a private sketch.

departure_2.narration: You choose an invitation for another reader first. The course warning must wait for the next relay.

return.narration: Your party and kit are back. The keepers lift the board; the island moves on freely. Pip watches the stone's empty eye vanish into cloud. Your checked clue shows land between these ridges was once joined. Its date and cause remain unknown.

variants.text: The first message is the course warning. The keeper logs its departure and waits for a reply.
The first message asks for another reader. The course warning waits for the next relay.
The messenger carries her dry letters and only the message you authorized.
The station cloths lift freely; its song slips remain dry.
Your independent test stays credited in the account.
The account credits the follow-up your party made with help, beside the first unfinished test.
The keeper stores your shared copy with its credit and limits.
Your private sketch stays with your party. The keeper files her own observations.
The extra kit relay leaves later than a light-kit crossing. Its delay stays in the log.

rest.narration: The board is stowed and the next watcher takes the bell rope. Your party rests on the grass. The old stone has given you a clue about the land below, and the moving island carries the original onward toward the temple route. You keep what you learned. The island keeps its stone. You can pause at the lookout or return to the whales' turning place before following the temple route.

landing_brace.narration: Your thornguard uses a skill called Brace to hold the board foot while the keeper secures its tie. The foot stays centered while she fastens the tie. The keepers still watch the gap as your party follows the side ropes across; no one is holding the islands in place.

letters_runner.narration: A duskrunner threads the recovery loop through the strap from the firm path. Pip steadies the pole. Their quick hands steady the pole, giving you a wider target for the lift. Nobody climbs beyond the fence, and the sealed letters stay closed.

letters_runner_check.narration: The mailbag hangs by its strap beside the fence. Reach with the looped pole from the marked ground. The letters are taking an unscheduled holiday.

interaction.cue: Tap when the marker reaches the gold.

sightings_whales.narration: The whales beyond the clear lane turn together. The keeper listens to their low note while your party sights the notch from the marked ground. The song tells you where to look first; you still need to confirm the fixed view. You do not call or ride the whales.

sightings_whales_check.narration: The whales you guided give the keeper a place to look. Wait for the notch to clear that patch of cloud, then check it against the fixed roof corner. The song helps the sighting; it cannot move the island.

interaction.cue: Check the notch in the whale-indicated clear interval.

comparison_clear.narration: Your clear copy distinguishes the old join from the crack. Use it for a wider scale check against the present sketch.

comparison_clear_check.narration: Your clear copy separates the old join from the later crack. That gives a wider interval for placing the scale; you still need to test it against the lookout sketch.

interaction.cue: Compare the clearly copied join with the present sketch.

comparison_recovery.narration: Two clear marks remain beside the worn patch. Compare them with the keeper holding a scale, or with Pip pointing from the viewing mark. The missing middle stays unanswered. Who will help your follow-up?

choices.label: Measure two clear marks with the keeper
Trace the two clear heights with Pip

comparison_recover_scale.narration: Your first measure stays unfinished. Support the keeper's scale for a different comparison of the clear outer marks. Leave the worn middle dotted.

interaction.cue: Hold the scale while the keeper checks the clear outer marks.

onSuccess.narration: The helped comparison is ready for your party to interpret.

onFailure.narration: Pip and the keeper hold the fixed reference together. You complete the helped comparison without filling the worn middle.

onAssisted.narration: The helped comparison is ready for your party to interpret.

comparison_recover_view.narration: Your first tracing stays unfinished. Share Pip's fixed view and the clear outer marks for a different comparison. Leave the worn middle dotted.

interaction.cue: Compare two clear heights without using the worn middle.

options.label: Pip points from the viewing mark

clues: Pip must point from the fixed viewing mark first.
Trace the clear outer marks before comparing their heights.
Leave the worn middle out of this follow-up.

onSuccess.narration: The helped comparison is ready for your party to interpret.

onFailure.narration: Pip and the keeper hold the fixed reference together. You complete the helped comparison without filling the worn middle.

onAssisted.narration: The helped comparison is ready for your party to interpret.

landing_recovery.narration: The keeper has a checked crossing, but your bulky kit is awkward in this wind. Borrow her pocket brush and sheet to keep the message relay's place; you will leave your broad copying frame behind. Or pass your complete kit in batches: more carrying, but the full frame comes with you and the message relay must wait. Which cost will you take?

choices.label: Carry the kit in batches; delay the message relay
Leave bulky gear and borrow the keeper's small kit

landing_batches.narration: Pass the complete kit in small loads along the checked board. Its broad frame will come with you. The extra carrying keeps your message relay waiting for the return.

interaction.cue: Pass each small load to the next helper.

onSuccess.narration: The complete kit reaches the island. Its larger tools remain available, but the message relay will leave later.

onFailure.narration: The complete kit reaches the island. Its larger tools remain available, but the message relay will leave later.

onAssisted.narration: The complete kit reaches the island. Its larger tools remain available, but the message relay will leave later.

landing_borrow.narration: Level the keeper's pocket tray, borrow its brush and sheet, then cross on her checked alignment. The small kit preserves the message slot. Your broad copying frame stays behind.

interaction.cue: Level the small borrowed tray before crossing.

onSuccess.narration: The small kit is across. The message relay keeps its place; the broad copying frame stays behind.

onFailure.narration: The small kit is across. The message relay keeps its place; the broad copying frame stays behind.

onAssisted.narration: The small kit is across. The message relay keeps its place; the broad copying frame stays behind.

whale_report.narration: Pass the whale-route page to the lookout keeper, checking its landmarks along the way. This delivers the report you promised. Your separate stone sketch stays private until you choose otherwise.

interaction.cue: Catch the route report, check a landmark, and pass it on.

onSuccess.narration: You have kept your promise to pass on the whale-route observations. Now decide separately what to do with the stone sketch.

variants.text: Your report says the whales followed the clear lane and left the paired openings ready.
Your report says the early opening scattered the whales. The keeper marks that the familiar whale signs may be missing.

camp.narration: The keeper brings ginger tea to the lookout roof while your party rests. Pip tries to weigh down a song slip with his cup, then remembers that he wants the tea. Outside, the island keeps its slow course. The landing board and signal cloths are ready for the next job.

carving_frame.narration: Your complete kit includes a broad frame that steadies the sheet beside the stone. Record the rounded carved edge without turning the sharp crack into a road.

interaction.cue: Copy the groove within the broad frame.

comparison_recover_scale_done.narration: With the keeper holding the scale, your outer marks fit the two ridges. The carved surface between them continues across today's gaps: the land was joined here. This is your helped follow-up. The worn middle stays dotted.

comparison_recover_view_done.narration: Pip supplies the fixed viewpoint while you trace the clear outer heights. The old surface continues across today's gaps: the land was joined here. You show the keeper the match. Your first tracing and its missing bend remain unfinished.

return_load.narration: The return gap is checked. Help pass the crew kit back, or take the light crossing if you borrowed a pocket kit. Any batch carrying must finish before its waiting message relay can leave.

choices.label: Help pass the crew kit back, then cross
Return with the borrowed pocket kit

return_kit.narration: Pass small kit loads to the lookout helpers while the keepers watch the gap. Follow the side ropes back when the receiving keeper calls. The island keeps moving freely.

interaction.cue: Pass the kit load to the next lookout helper.

onSuccess.narration: The last kit load and your whole party reach the lookout.

onFailure.narration: The last kit load and your whole party reach the lookout.

onAssisted.narration: The last kit load and your whole party reach the lookout.

return_light.narration: The pocket brush and folded sheet leave your hands free for the side ropes. Keep the board supported as the last helper returns with the light tray.

interaction.cue: Steady the return board for the light kit.

onSuccess.narration: Your party returns with the pocket kit. You give the brush back to its keeper.

onFailure.narration: Your party returns with the pocket kit. You give the brush back to its keeper.

onAssisted.narration: Your party returns with the pocket kit. You give the brush back to its keeper.

dispatch.narration: You are back at the lookout with the authorized temple message. Prepare a hand relay, or use the station or messenger whose slot you preserved. The private stone sketch stays separate.

choices.label: Prepare and pass the authorized hand-relay message
Give the authorized message to the ready messenger

message_pack.narration: A hand relay needs a clear packet even if another helper could carry it. Put the lookout sender, temple destination and authorized message together so each watcher knows exactly what may be passed.

interaction.cue: Prepare the hand relay's dispatch.
clues: Name who is sending before choosing a destination.
The temple destination goes before the message it should receive.
Include only the message your party authorized.

onSuccess.narration: The relay has its sender, destination and authorized message.

onFailure.narration: The keeper checks the packet with you. Its private-sketch space stays empty.

onAssisted.narration: The relay has its sender, destination and authorized message.

message_hand.narration: Pass the authorized packet along the lookout's waiting line. The keeper logs when it leaves rather than claiming an answer has already arrived.

interaction.cue: Catch and pass the authorized temple packet.

onSuccess.narration: The hand-relay packet leaves with only the authorized message.

onFailure.narration: The hand-relay packet leaves with only the authorized message.

onAssisted.narration: The hand-relay packet leaves with only the authorized message.

message_frame.narration: Your ready station still has its dispatch slot. Pass the cloth message to the next lookout watcher while the keeper confirms its meaning. The flag does not carry a private drawing.

interaction.cue: Hold the station cloth while the keeper reads the message.

onSuccess.narration: The keeper logs the station dispatch and waits for a reply.

onFailure.narration: The keeper logs the station dispatch and waits for a reply.

onAssisted.narration: The keeper logs the station dispatch and waits for a reply.

message_messenger.narration: The dry letter bag and saved departure slot are ready. Pass the authorized temple message to the messenger, leaving the stone sketch with its chosen owner.

interaction.cue: Pass only the authorized message to the messenger.

onSuccess.narration: The messenger takes the authorized message with her dry letters.

onFailure.narration: The messenger takes the authorized message with her dry letters.

onAssisted.narration: The messenger takes the authorized message with her dry letters.
